# lyrn

> Start a new web application on the lacodda line's stack with one command - one stack assembled to the end, and a repository ready to work in from the first commit.

lyrn is a Rust command-line tool. `lyrn new` generates a repository in one of
nine forms, `lyrn adopt` brings an existing one up to the same standard, and
`lyrn template` checks or exports templates. Everything below is written for
people and agents alike: there is no second set of instructions kept elsewhere.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what it is, how to install it, what working with it looks like
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): the gate to run before a commit, where things live, how commits are written
- [Architecture decisions](docs/adr/README.md): why it is built the way it is, one decision per file
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): what each release changed
- [Documentation site](https://lyrn.lacodda.com/llms.txt): every page of the manual, in the form an agent reads

## Optional

- [Security policy](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability, privately
